research_rationale: EO 11298 (signed 1966-08-14; 31 FR 10915) is a single paragraph in which the President prescribes, under 10 U.S.C. 1035 as amended by the Act of August 14, 1966, ten percent per annum, compounded quarterly, as the interest rate on amounts deposited by members of the uniformed services, and states that the order is effective September 1, 1966. I read the complete held Federal Register text. The dossier inventory of one clause covers the whole order and I confirmed it without correction. The effective-date sentence fixes a start, not an end, and no sunset or ending condition appears. A search of the held texts for the order's number finds only the order's own Federal Register page and the 1989 codification entry, which lists no amendment or revocation. The three bounded machine searches record no adverse disposition. The clause is therefore treated as operative on the original text through 2026-10-14. Whether the statute still authorizes the rate was not read from held statute text; that is a limit of the bounded-search basis and is not claimed as quoted authority.
savings_reason: The order contains no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause and nothing held ends it, so no residual effect arises.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end: the only dated sentence is the effective date of September 1, 1966, which starts the rate. No held instrument revokes, supersedes or amends the order.
scope_check: The whole order is one paragraph, one command (the interest rate), and it is the single clause in the inventory.
independent_command_check: There is one command, so no independent command can survive or end separately.
savings_check: None found in the order; nothing survives an end because no end is shown.

research_rationale: EO 12598 (signed 1987-06-17; 52 FR 23421) implements Title VIII of the Omnibus Diplomatic Security and Antiterrorism Act of 1986 (Public Law 99-399). Sections 1 and 2 delegate presidential functions under section 803(a) to the Secretary of State (section 2 in consultation with the Secretary of Labor); sections 3 and 4 delegate functions under section 806 to the Secretary of Defense (section 4 in consultation with the Secretary of Labor); section 5 directs the Secretaries of State and Defense to consult with each other and other agencies; section 6 supersedes Executive Order No. 12576. I read the complete held Federal Register text. The dossier inventory of six clauses, one per section, covers the whole order and I confirmed it without correction. No section has a fixed end. Section 6 acts on another instrument and was performed on issuance, so I record it as spent on the order's date; its own effect on EO 12576 survives in that order's absence. A search of the held texts for the number finds only the order's own page and the 1989 codification entry, which lists no amendment or revocation, and the three bounded machine searches record no adverse disposition. Sections 1 to 5 are therefore operative on the original text through 2026-10-14. The statute and CFR text the searches point to are not held as quoted text and are not relied on as authority.
savings_reason: Section 6's supersession of Executive Order No. 12576 is a performed act whose effect (that order no longer operating) continues independently of this order; the order has no savings clause and nothing held ends sections 1 to 5, so no other residual arises.
earlier_end_check: No section has an own-terms end. Section 6 is the only clause with a dated, self-executing effect and it is recorded as spent on the order's date. No held instrument revokes, supersedes or amends the order.
scope_check: Sections 1 to 4 are separate delegations to the named Secretaries; section 5 is a consultation duty for State and Defense; section 6 acts only on EO 12576. None is limited in time or place.
independent_command_check: The four delegations and the consultation duty do not depend on one another to continue; section 6's performance does not affect them.
savings_check: Section 6's supersession is an accrued effect on EO 12576, not a continuing command of this order; no other savings.

research_rationale: EO 10863 (signed 1960-02-18; 25 FR 1507) designates the Attorney General, under section 1 of Title VI of the act of June 15, 1917 as amended (22 U.S.C. 401), as the person authorized to seize and detain arms and munitions of war, other articles and vessels, vehicles or aircraft used in illegal export (section 1), and lets any officer of the Department of Justice designated by the Attorney General exercise that authority (section 2). I read the complete held Federal Register text; the held file also reprints the next order on the page (EO 10864), which is not part of this order and is the only reason the number appears in a second held file. The dossier inventory is one clause spanning sections 1 and 2; I confirmed that it covers every command of the order. The order has no sunset or ending condition. A search of the held texts for the number finds no other instrument that cites it apart from that page overlap and the 1989 codification entry, which lists no amendment or revocation, and the three bounded machine searches record no adverse disposition. The clause is operative on the original text through 2026-10-14. The statute and CFR text the searches point to are not held as quoted text and are not relied on as authority.
savings_reason: The order has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause and nothing held ends it, so no residual effect arises.
earlier_end_check: No own-terms end: sections 1 and 2 state no date, condition or term. No held instrument revokes, supersedes or amends the order.
scope_check: The clause covers the Attorney General's designation (section 1) and the delegation to designated Department of Justice officers (section 2), both without limit in time.
independent_command_check: Section 2's delegation depends on section 1's authority; both continue together, and no independent command was found to end earlier.
